findings.title: Cache check-then-act race allows concurrent manifest reloads and duplicate work
findings.body: GetWebAssets performs a read-lock check of entryPointAssetsCache (lines 41-43), releases the lock, and then re-acquires a write lock (line 48) to recompute the cache. Between the RUnlock and Lock, another goroutine can also pass the nil check and enter the write-lock section, so multiple goroutines can concurrently execute readWebAssetsFromFile/readWebAssetsFromCDN and overwrite entryPointAssetsCache. This is not a data race on the pointer itself (the mutex does protect the read/write of the variable), but it is a check-then-act race: in non-dev environments the cache is supposed to be computed once, yet N concurrent first-callers will all perform file I/O (or an HTTP request to the CDN) and each will assign the global. Consequences: wasted work, potential thundering-herd file/HTTP load on startup, and last-writer-wins assignment of the cache. The fix is a double-checked locking pattern: after acquiring the write lock, re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` before doing the expensive work.

findings.title: Error from asset loading is discarded when cache is assigned and returned
findings.body: At line 69-70, `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is assigned unconditionally and then `return entryPointAssetsCache, err` returns both the (possibly nil) result and the error. If readWebAssetsFromFile fails (e.g., assets-manifest.json missing or malformed), result is nil and err is non-nil, but the nil result is still stored into the package-level cache. On the next call in a non-dev environment, the fast path at line 45 (`cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil`) will see ret == nil and retry — which is arguably intended — but in dev mode the cache is overwritten with nil on every failed call, and more importantly the function returns a nil *dtos.EntryPointAssets together with a non-nil error while having mutated global state. Callers that ignore the error (or that only check the returned pointer) could dereference nil. Additionally, if a previous successful result existed and a later reload fails, the good cached value is clobbered with nil. The assignment should be conditional on err == nil (or result != nil), e.g. `if err == nil { entryPointAssetsCache = result }`.

findings.title: CDN read error is silently overwritten by file read, losing the original error
findings.body: Lines 55-67: when `cdn != ""`, `result, err = readWebAssetsFromCDN(ctx, cdn)` is called. If that fails, err is set and result is nil, then line 59 `if result == nil` falls through to readWebAssetsFromFile, which overwrites err. If the file read succeeds, the CDN error is completely lost and the function returns success — fine for fallback semantics, but if the file read also fails, the returned error describes only the file failure, not the CDN failure, making it impossible to diagnose why CDN loading was attempted and failed. More subtly, the CDN path is currently dead code (cdn is hardcoded to "" at line 54), so this error-masking behavior is latent. If/when the CDN is enabled, the error handling should preserve or wrap both errors (e.g., using errors.Join or logging the CDN error) rather than silently discarding it.
